blindSummary: The country's largest LGBTQ+ community and its biggest police raids coexist here, with police acting without legal basis. (1) 1 February 2025: police arrested 56 men at a hotel in the capital at a reported "gay sex party"; organisers risk pornography-law prosecution with penalties up to 15 years; an international human-rights NGO called the police's "discriminatory and senseless harassment of LGBTI people ... has no basis in law" and demanded release of those detained. (2) One of the eight states/provinces where an international NGO found discriminatory regional regulations — and simultaneously the city with the country's densest LGBTQ+ infrastructure, media presence and monitoring-group offices; expect both to be true at once. National climate from this record's sources: an October 2025 presidential decree listed "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among the country's non-military national security threats alongside terrorism and drugs, amplifying self-censorship (editors killing LGBTQ+ stories for fear of state reprisal); police deny violence and extortions in the 2022 death-in-custody of a trans activist based abroad arrested on drug charges at an airport while family members allege he was beaten. The sheer scale of the community limits enforcement reach.
